displayedInputs.question: Given \(f(x)=x^3-3x\), what is the positive value of \(x\) for which \(f'(x)=0\)?
Given \(f(x)=2x^3\), what is \(f'(1)\)?
What is the degree of the derivative of a cubic polynomial?
To travel from location A to location B, there are 3 bus services and 2 train services. The two types cannot be taken simultaneously. How many ways are there to travel in total?
There are 4 mathematics books and 5 Chinese language books on a bookshelf. If only 1 book is selected, how many ways are there to select it?
In which situation does the addition principle of counting apply?

choices.A: Every category must be carried out once
choices.B: Several categories of ways are mutually exclusive, and completing the task requires choosing a way from just one category
choices.C: Each step must be followed by the next step
choices.D: A way may belong to two categories simultaneously, and the counts are still added

displayedInputs.question: 6 people signed up for singing and 4 people signed up for dancing. No one signed up for both. How many people signed up in total?
There are 3 tops and 4 pairs of pants. How many outfits can be made by choosing 1 top and 1 pair of pants?
There are 2 roads from A to B and 3 roads from B to C. How many ways are there to travel from A through B to C?
In which situation does the multiplication principle of counting apply?

choices.A: Completing just one of the steps is sufficient
choices.B: The numbers of ways for the individual steps should be added
choices.C: Every step must be completed in order for the task to be complete
choices.D: The steps can be reversed into mutually exclusive categories

displayedInputs.question: A password has three digits. Each digit can be any of the 10 digits from 0 to 9, and repetition is allowed. How many passwords are there in total?
Choose 1 representative from 3 boys and 2 girls, then choose 1 of 4 notebooks to give to the representative. How many ways are there to do this?
To travel to Beijing, you can take one of 2 flights or 3 high-speed trains. After arriving, you choose 1 of 4 hotels. How many arrangements are possible?
You first choose transportation, then a hotel. There are two categories of transportation: flights and high-speed trains. How should you count the possibilities?

choices.A: Add all the numbers of transportation options and hotels
choices.C: Multiply the number of flights by the number of high-speed trains, then add the number of hotels
choices.D: Add the numbers of transportation options, then multiply by the number of hotels

displayedInputs.question: There are 2 breakfast options and 3 lunch options. How many combinations are possible if you choose 1 breakfast and 1 lunch?
Which of the following is a permutation?

choices.A: Choose 2 of 4 students to form a group, without regard to order
choices.B: Put 4 books into a pile, without distinguishing left from right
choices.C: Choose 2 of 4 students and arrange them in order
choices.D: Consider only which people were selected

displayedInputs.question: Choose 2 from 4 distinct elements and arrange them in a row. How many arrangements are there?
The letters A, B, and C are all distinct. Arrange all of them in a row. How many arrangements are there?
What conditions must be met for two permutations to be identical?

choices.A: Only the selected elements need to be the same
choices.B: The selected elements and their order must both be the same
choices.C: Only the number of elements needs to be the same
choices.D: Only the first position needs to be the same

displayedInputs.question: What is \(A(6,2)\)?
What is \(A(5,1)\)?
What is \(A(4,4)\)?
Which is one way to express \(A(n,k)\)?

choices.A: The factorial of \(n\) multiplied by the factorial of \(k\)
choices.B: The factorial of \(k\) divided by the factorial of \(n\)
choices.C: The factorial of \(n\) divided by the factorial of \((n-k)\)

displayedInputs.question: 5 students stand in a row for a photograph, with every student included. How many arrangements are there?
From 7 distinct books, give 1 book each to 3 people, A, B, and C. How many ways are there to do this?
How many three-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, and 4, with each digit used at most once?
Give 3 distinct books to 3 distinct people, with each person receiving 1 book. What type of counting is this?

choices.A: A combination of choosing 1 book from 3 books
choices.B: Adding the numbers of the 3 books

displayedInputs.question: Which of the following is a combination?

choices.A: Selecting 2 from 4 students and arranging them in a line
choices.B: Selecting 2 from 4 students to attend a meeting, without regard to order
choices.C: Forming a three-digit number using 3 distinct digits
choices.D: Arranging 5 people in a line with distinct front-to-back positions

displayedInputs.question: Choose 2 from 4 distinct elements, without regard to order. How many selections are there?
Select 2 from 5 students for classroom duty, without regard to who comes first or second. How many selections are there?
If a group of elements is merely reordered, how should it be counted as a combination?

choices.A: It is still the same combination
choices.C: It becomes the factorial of the number of permutations
choices.D: It can no longer be called a combination

displayedInputs.question: What is \(C(6,2)\)?
What is \(C(5,0)\)?
What is the relationship between \(C(n,k)\) and \(A(n,k)\)?

choices.A: The number of combinations equals the number of permutations multiplied by \(k\)
choices.B: The number of combinations equals the number of permutations divided by the factorial of \(k\)
choices.C: The number of combinations equals the factorial of \(n\)

displayedInputs.question: Given that \(C(8,3)=C(8,5)\), what is \(C(8,5)\)?
Which of the following equals \(C(n,k)\)?
3 students are selected from 6 students to participate in an activity, without regard to order. How many ways are there to select them?
